title: A planet that makes its own magnet
learning_goal: Understand that the field must be regenerated by moving liquid metal, that a dynamo is a self-amplifying loop with a threshold, and that physics prefers neither polarity.
takeaway: A moving conducting fluid can turn a tiny field into a large one once its loop gain passes a threshold, and the laws do not prefer north or south.
notes: The T4 chapter card plays in the 3.2-s lead-in of 01.1 (no separate scene id), without the staircase, which first appears at the end of L1. Predict beats: Q1 in 01.3 (hold 3.0 s), Q2 in 01.5 (hold 2.5 s); on screen they read PREDICT only, to avoid a clash with the question-card numbers (ASK · Q2 is this chapter's card). External facts (core layers, age of the field, cut magnet, bicycle generator, acoustic feedback, self-exciting disc) carry a reference lower-third or chip and a dated source (BRIEF D7). Badges: CONTEXT for sourced facts and analogies, PROVED for the energy budget (P3 Theorem 3.3) and the B -> -B invariance (P3:239), none on the recap and the question card. The decay argument replaces the Curie temperature (critique C4); lines never start or stop, without 'close on themselves' (B4); s is the growth rate (D1). 01.3 plants 'just past the threshold, growth is slow' and 01.5 'the seed's sign decides', which the question card ch01.Q uses. 01.6 target raised from 12 to 13 s to end on the open question 'no wires in liquid iron' (P3:1399). Words budgeted at about 127.5 effective words per minute against target_s; estimates use the assembler formula (146 raw words per minute, 0.9 s per paragraph break, holds, lead-in and tail). Adversarial review 2026-11-08: changes and evidence in script/_review/ch01.md (01.5 now asks before it shows the symmetry). CONSISTENCY EDITOR (2026-11-08): badge notes added to 01.4 and 01.5 (from params.badge_note); ch01.Q keeps Q2 in the register numbering.

scenes.title: No magnet inside

chapter.title: A planet that makes its own magnet

sentences.text: Is there a giant magnet hidden inside the Earth?
Deep down, the outer core is an ocean of liquid iron.
Left alone, a {b}field{/} there would fade away within tens of thousands of years.
Yet Earth's field is several billion years old.
So the moving iron must keep making it, all the time.

scenes.title: Lines never end

box_rests: the north end of the right half

sentences.text: Take a bar magnet: north at one end, south at the other.
Cut it in half.
You get two magnets, each with a north and a south.
No one has ever found a lone magnetic pole.
{b}Field lines{/} say the same: they never start or stop.
Draw any box, and count.
As many lines go in as come out.
Keep this box in mind.

labels: field lines never start or stop

formulas.tex: \nabla\cdot\B = 0 \iff \oint_{\partial V}\B\cdot\mathrm{d}\mathbf{S} = 0\ \text{ for every closed surface } \partial V

chips: REFERENCE · Univ. of Illinois Physics Van 2008 · cutting a magnet
REFERENCE · no isolated magnetic pole ever observed · P1 §3.3

scenes.title: The squeal

params.note: illustrative ratios only: no number of these is ever shown on screen (SCHEMATIC)

sentences.text: A bicycle dynamo turns motion into electricity, using a built-in magnet.
The Earth has to make its own. The trick: a loop.
Hold a microphone near its own speaker, and turn up the {param}gain{/}.
Below a certain point, a whisper fades.
Past it, the loop feeds itself.
Now spin a copper disc wired to a coil around its axle.
Current makes {b}field{/}, and field makes current.
Spin it faster and faster. Does the field grow bit by bit, or not at all until some speed?
Not at all, until a threshold.
Past it, each turn multiplies a tiny {b}seed field{/} by the same factor: exponential growth.
Just past the threshold, growth is slow.
Then the field brakes the disc, and growth stops.

labels: Does the field grow bit by bit, or not at all until some speed?

formulas.tex: L_c\,\dot I + R_c\,I = \frac{\cp{\Omega}\,M}{2\pi}\,I \;\Rightarrow\; I \propto e^{s t},\qquad s = \Big(\frac{\cp{\Omega}\,M}{2\pi} - R_c\Big)\Big/ L_c

chips: REFERENCE · bicycle generator with a permanent magnet · Chiu 2004, US patent 6,703,716
REFERENCE · acoustic feedback · van Waterschoot & Moonen 2010
REFERENCE · self-exciting disc · Bullard 1955 · P3 exercise 2

scenes.title: Who pays the bill

sentences.text: Who pays for all this?
A motor drives the {u}flow{/}; in the Earth, convection does.
The flow stretches the field; the field brakes the flow.
Once growth stops, every watt that goes in leaves as heat, on average.
A dynamo turns motion into field; it creates no energy.

labels: on average: power in = heat out

formulas.tex: \mathbb{E}\big[\langle \U\cdot\mathbf{f}\rangle\big] = \nu\,\mathbb{E}\big[\langle|\boldsymbol{\omega}|^{2}\rangle\big] + \etaP\,\mathbb{E}\big[\langle|\mathbf{j}|^{2}\rangle\big]\quad \text{(steady regime: holds for the distribution, not for each snapshot)}

On 'heat': two dashed grey arrows drop from the boxes into the tray, 'friction in the fluid' under 'flow' and 'electric heating' under 'field'; tokens now leave into the tray at the same average rate as they arrive from the motor (no counter on screen), and the dashed-outline tag 'on average: power in = heat out' appears under the tray (the dashed 'on average' tag style of 00.4). scenes.title: Which way is up?

sentences.text: Earth's {b}field{/} points one way today. Which way should it prefer?
Reverse every field line: the dynamo's equations read the same.
So, neither. The two directions are mirror twins, equally lawful.
Which one you get is history, not law: in the disc, the seed's sign decides.
And nothing in the laws forbids a flip.

labels: Which way should the field prefer to point?

formulas.tex: \partial_t\B = \nabla\times(\U\times\B) + \etaP\,\Delta\B\ \text{ is linear in }\B,\ \ \mathbf{j}\times\B\ \text{ is quadratic: MHD is invariant under }\ \B\to-\B

scenes.visual: Render class flat. On 'prefer-0.15': a grey Earth disc (radius about 200 px, centred, y about 600) wrapped in vermillion dipole field lines with arrowheads, as in 00.2 but flat, and the PREDICT card slides in at the top, 'Which way should the field prefer to point?', with two grey outline buttons 'north' and 'south' under it (predict beat Q2 of the outline; the 2.5 s hold comes from the script; the viewer guesses before the symmetry is shown). During the hold nothing new appears; the field lines breathe. On 'reverse-0.15': the card shrinks to the top edge at 60 % opacity, buttons still visible; every arrowhead swings round along its line and the shade swaps from --b to --b-neg (1.0 s morph), holds 1 s, then swings back to --b (0.6 s); the label 'same equations' appears with a pen check mark (M9). No equation on the main layer. On 'neither': both buttons light equally and the pen draws one underline under both; the card slides up and out; the mirror (M10, first appearance, Kit.mirror mode 'plane', only as the B → −B metaphor) rises as a vertical plane at x 960; the Earth moves to the left half and its twin appears in the right half: same line shapes, arrows reversed, shade --b-neg; label 'B → −B: same equations' above the mirror, 'mirror twins' below it. On 'history': under each twin a short vermillion growth curve from 01.3 is drawn from a tiny seed arrow, one going up from '+ seed' (--b) under the left twin, one going down from '− seed' (--b-neg) under the right twin: the sign of the seed is kept as it grows. On 'forbid-0.15': the compass needle (M1, Kit.needle corner false, size 240 px) appears on the mirror line between the twins and swings 180 degrees (flip at 'forbid+0.5', overshoot at most 3 %, needle sound); as it turns, the left twin dims to 50 % and the right twin brightens to 100 %. Grey dashed chip SCHEMATIC on the twins (a metaphor; the real symmetry acts on the field, not on a picture). Badge PROVED top-right with the note params.badge_note. question.en: Near the threshold, should dynamo simulations start from a *tiny seed*, a strong one, or *both*?
question.fr: Près du seuil, les simulations de dynamo doivent-elles partir d'un germe minuscule, d'un germe fort, ou des deux ?
question.why: Near threshold a tiny seed grows slowly and may not saturate within the run; a strong seed may reach a subcritical dynamo that a tiny one misses.
question.unblocks: Seed amplitude (now 10⁻³) and length of the Taylor–Green runs; whether the data need branch labels.
question.why_fr: Près du seuil, un germe minuscule croît lentement et peut ne pas saturer pendant la simulation ; un germe fort peut atteindre une dynamo sous-critique qu'un germe minuscule manque.
question.unblocks_fr: Amplitude du germe (aujourd'hui 10⁻³) et durée des simulations Taylor–Green ; étiquetage éventuel des branches dans les données.
